chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, he said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to us, he said: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yasar al-Thawri narrated to us, he said: al-Khalil ibn Rashid narrated to us, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said:

I accompanied Abul Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far from Mecca to Medina. One day he said to me: 'O Ali, if the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth revolted against the Banu al-Abbas, the earth would be watered with their blood until al-Sufyani rises.' I said to him: 'O my master, is his rising inevitable?' He said: 'Yes.' Then he pondered for a while, then raised his head and said: 'The rule of the Banu al-Abbas is based on cunning and deceit. It will pass until it is said that nothing of it remains, then it will return until it is said that nothing like it has ever happened.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Musa al-Kadhim say about the nature of Abbasid rule and the rise of al-Sufyani?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kadhim (as) highlights the strategic patience of the Ahl al-Bayt amidst the Abbasid caliphate, characterizing their rule as a period of 'cunning and deceit' that will eventually collapse and be replaced by the rise of al-Sufyani. This narration underscores the Shia eschatological view that the current political order is transient and divinely ordained to pave the way for the final victory of the Mahdi.
